activities.anchor: Two creeds had been building for thirty years
activities.caption: pair each creed with its programme
activities.name: rev1848CreedsMatch

config.prompt: Two creeds under the Congress system — pair each with its programme:

pairs.right: written constitutions, free press, jury trial, careers open to talent rather than birth
who is 'the people'? — Herder's Volksgeist, folk epics, dictionaries, Hungarian language-laws
Spain, Naples, Greece, France, Belgium, Poland, Kraków — rehearsals; each failed and each taught
whose nation governs in Bohemia, Hungary, the Balkans?

config.why: The two creeds were natural allies — both opposed the dynasts and the 1815 settlement — but in the multi-national empires the fault line would open underfoot in 1848.

activities.anchor: Ideas explain the demands; the harvest explains the timing
activities.caption: call the multiple — the economic fuse
activities.name: rev1848FuseEstimate

config.prompt: The 1846–47 grain failures sent food prices to roughly what multiple of their normal levels in many cities?
config.why: Double their normal levels — bread riots were already the routine of 1847 in Berlin and Vienna, and the 1847 financial and industrial slump threw artisans out of work precisely when bread cost most.
config.context: Railways carried news and strikers faster than cavalry; telegraph wires carried Paris's outcome to Vienna in days.

activities.anchor: Strip the local costumes and 1848 repeats a script
activities.caption: file each episode under its act
activities.name: rev1848ActsBuckets

config.prompt: The three-act pattern — file each episode:

items.label: barricades, National Guard mutinies, a palace concession
the Second Republic founded with universal male suffrage — the first in Europe since 1793
Germans elect the Frankfurt Parliament to the Paulskirche
Hungarians win the April Laws from Vienna
the government closes the national workshops; some 100,000 workers rise
General Cavaignac crushes the June Days — 1,500 dead in four days

config.why: The June Days are 1848's hinge and its symbol: the 'springtime of peoples' had split into two peoples, and after June the propertied classes everywhere began asking the old regimes for protection.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — five reasons, ranked
activities.name: rev1848FailSpot

config.prompt: One line of this failure analysis is wrong — click it:
lines: German liberals wanted a greater Germany including Bohemia; Palacký refused Frankfurt — 'I am a Czech of Slav blood'.
In Hungary, the Croats, Serbs and Romanians fought for Budapest against Vienna.
Windischgrätz bombarded Prague (June) and stormed Vienna (31 October).
Tsar Nicholas I sent some 200,000 troops into Hungary in June 1849; the Hungarian army broke at Világos.
Frankfurt's offer of the imperial crown to Frederick William IV (April 1849) was refused — 'a crown from the gutter'.
config.correction: The Magyar revolution under Kossuth alienated Croats, Serbs and Romanians — who fought for Vienna against Budapest.
config.why: The minorities feared each other's nation-state more than the emperor's empire: the revolutions cancelled each other, and the dynasties' survival was a coalition achievement.

activities.anchor: a parliament elected to write a constitution had no army
activities.caption: true or false — 1848's misreadings
activities.name: rev1848MarxJudge

statements.s: The Communist Manifesto, printed days before Paris rose, organised almost nobody in the barricades.
statements.why: The barricades demanded constitutions, press freedom and national unification.

statements.s: Marx led the revolution of 1848 from the barricades.
statements.why: He spent 1848 editing a Cologne newspaper and then theorising the defeat — the revolution's analyst, never its leader.

statements.s: The social question surfaced violently only once in 1848 — the June Days.
statements.why: Where the republic's own workers fought the republic.

statements.s: The Frankfurt Parliament failed solely because one king refused a crown.
statements.why: It had no army, no revenue, and no agreed answer on whether Austria belonged inside the Germany it was drafting — the refusal was the staging, not the cause.

activities.caption: file each deposit under its class
activities.name: rev1848StuckBuckets

config.prompt: What changed anyway — file each deposit:

items.label: universal male suffrage in France — the December 1848 election proved democracy durable and dangerous
Habsburg serfdom, abolished September 1848, never restored
Prussia kept a constitution and an elected Landtag
Cavour's moral: unification needs a great-power ally and a dynastic engine (1859–61)
Bismarck: 'not by speeches and majority votes… but by iron and blood' (1862)
the Forty-Eighters emigrated by the tens of thousands, carrying nationalism abroad
the trade-union and socialist movements of the 1860s — June Days' children

config.why: Hobsbawm's verdict is the standard one: as a defeat, 1848 was the century's most productive — it ended the 'dual revolution''s first act and opened its second.

activities.caption: line up the verdicts, by generation
activities.name: rev1848VerdictOrder

config.prompt: One 'failure', four verdicts — order them by generation, earliest first:
items: the Kreuzzeitung's obituary: 'the fools' year' — written by 1848's own generation
Marx theorises the defeat in the Eighteenth Brumaire (1852) — 'first as tragedy, then as farce'
1871 crowns the lost liberal nationalisms — 1848 re-cast as prophecy rather than fiasco
modern social historians (Rapport, Hobsbawm): the moment politics became mass politics
config.why: The exam skill is to date your verdict's lens: 'failure' from the barricades, 'turning point' from the 1870s, 'democratic breakthrough' from ours.

activities.anchor: The residual puzzle is Britain's absence
activities.caption: February 1848: you govern another capital — decide
activities.name: rev1848CapitalBranch

config.root: February 1848: barricades end Louis-Philippe's monarchy in seventy-two hours. You govern another capital, and the news arrives in days. Decide.

start.text: Paris's rising is proof of concept, as every capital reads it. Your calculation?

choices.label: Concede now — constitution and press freedom
choices.feedback: Most conceded: constitutions in Prussia and the Austrian lands, press freedom everywhere, national parliaments summoned in Frankfurt and Budapest.

choices.label: Gamble the throne
choices.feedback: The counter-attack took two years to reconquer what had been surrendered in two weeks — where the armies obeyed.

concede.text: Your concession holds — but the question the revolution deferred is coming: what does the new order owe the poor?

choices.label: Watch the June Days with alarm
choices.feedback: After June, the propertied classes everywhere began asking the old regimes for protection.

gamble.text: Your armies mostly held — Windischgrätz bombarded Prague and stormed Vienna, and the Tsar's 200,000 troops rescued the Habsburgs in Hungary.

choices.label: Count the cost
choices.feedback: The gamble worked only where the soldiers obeyed — and 1848's final entry is a legacy, not an event: Louis-Napoleon's Second Empire.

end.text: Liberty everywhere in February; its defeat nearly everywhere by 1849 — the year's outcome stays confusable until you keep the timeline in front of you.

config.why: The calculation every government faced was identical: concede now or gamble the throne.
